name: Sodium dodecylphosphate
description: Sodium dodecylphosphate ( CAS 50957-96-5 ), also known as Sodium lauryl phosphate, is an anionic surfactant derived from lauryl alcohol and phosphoric acid. It delivers effective surface-active performance across personal care and industrial formulations. This chemical is highly valued where mildness and emulsification are priorities. In personal care, it functions as a cleansing and emulsifying agent in shampoos, facial cleansers, and body washes for consumers. It offers a milder profile than conventional sulfate-based surfactants. Household and industrial cleaning formulations use it to degrease hard surfaces and stabilize emulsified soil suspensions in liquid detergent systems. Textile processing operations employ it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove oils and sizing agents from fiber substrates before dyeing. This ensures a high-quality finish for various fabric types. In leather and paper processing, it supports emulsification of treatment baths and improves penetration of finishing agents into substrate surfaces. This versatility makes it a staple in heavy industrial manufacturing. Sodium dodecylphosphate is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, with concentration levels varying by grade and intended application. Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material are available in the market. Cosmetic grades meet specific purity requirements for personal care use.
